Should US teachers be paid more?

No. There is an over-supply of teachers currently. It's a pretty easy job and someone can be trained quickly and easily to do it. The requirements to earn an education degree are low and the classes are extremely easy.
Good teachers should be paid more, not all teachers are good teachers. We need a way to identify the good ones and make certain they're paid more.

I propose we could have a system where there is a principle teacher that has seniority over the rest in the school. That person can decide, within budget constraints, who should be given a raise or not as time progresses. Of course, there would be normal cost of living adjustments applied school wide, but merit raises would be decided by this principle teacher.

The principle teacher, would be administrated by a senior principle teacher that was super senior. The super senior principle would administer the others, and answer to the county or district senior senior principle teacher.

This system would go all the way to state, then national with each higher rank showing more ability to recognize talent and ability. This way those who know teaching would decide, instead of an internet message board.
I don't think one teacher should be in charge of deciding who gets raises - there is potential for grudges and favors affecting who gets raises instead of actual merit.
In cases where the the principle teacher is showing favoritism, the super principle would receive a grievance from the teachers affected by the favoritism and the principle teacher would be replaced.

In the private sector they call it "competition". The sucky restaurants fail and the good ones make money.

There is no democratic way to do this, except by wallet.
Yes, to account for the higher degree of qualifications we should require of them.

Absolutely! This should be a well paid and highly valued (and respected*) career that attracts the best of the best. Our children deserve this.

I'll admit it. I'm a distro hopper. I never stay with a distro long (ubuntu being the longest at 8 months) because I like trying everything linux has to offer. When I do a fresh install I always manually set my partitions. 

500 Gb total on my harddrive
ESP - 200 mb
SWAP - 6 Gb
Ext4 as / - 30 Gb
Btrfs as /home - remaining

How does everyone else partition? Personal preferences? Do you let the distro choose? Any tips for the younger penguins?

Here is mine. Nothing fancy except that partitions are block aligned. No Btrfs at the moment as I have no use for journaling on this machine.

@> lsblk -o NAME,FSTYPE,SIZE,MOUNTPOINT
NAME FSTYPE SIZE MOUNTPOINT
sda 698.7G 
├─sda1 488M 
├─sda2 ext4 18.6G /
├─sda3 ext4 9.3G /var
├─sda4 ext4 477M /boot
├─sda5 swap 7.5G [SWAP]
└─sda6 ext4 662.3G /home

I just do what the distro decides, unless I'm building a server. I only single boot and if I do try another distro, it's always the only one. One thing though, you should have more swap than that. 2-4 GB is fine for most uses, but it is used for things besides just when you run out of RAM. Linux was built to utilize swap not only as a last resort, but as another tool in the old tool box.

I know swap is slower than ram, but faster than a bottleneck; Would swap be more efficient sharing a small SSD with / ?

Edit: on a more complex configuration, with more than just /home on a larger HD.

Like I said, your system will use swap naturally, when it feels it is best, not just when you are running low on RAM. If you have an SSD and spinning metal, it should go on the SSD.
